To find his speed in miles per hour we divide the number of miles he runs by the number of hours he runs so 20 / 1.5 = 13.33. To find his speed in miles per hour we round the number to the nearest whole number so 13.33 becomes 13. So the answer is 13.

In one hour, she can walk at a speed that is half as fast as she can run, so she can walk at a speed of 12 / 2 = 6 miles per hour. In six hours, she spends one - third of the time walking, which is 6 / 3 = 2 hours. During this time, she can walk 6 miles per hour * 2 hours = 12 miles. She also spends one - third of the time running, which is also 2 hours. During this time, she can run at a speed of 12 miles per hour * 2 hours = 24 miles. In total, over the six hours, she can run 24 miles + walk 12 miles = 36 miles. So the answer is 36.

Since a 60-gram serving has 60 calories, you can eat 200 / 60 = 3.33 servings. Since you can't consume a fraction of a serving, you can eat a maximum of 3 servings. Since each serving is 60 grams, you can eat a maximum of 3 * 60 = 180 grams. So the answer is 180.

Charlie makes 10 candles for 1 pound of beeswax, so he makes 10 * 10 = 100 dollars from making candles. The cost of the beeswax and wicks is 10 dollars, so his net profit is 100 - 10 = 90 dollars. If he sells 20 candles, his total revenue is 20 * 2 = 40 dollars. His net profit is 40 - 10 = 30 dollars. So the answer is 30.

On Wednesday, she wrote twice the number of articles she wrote on Tuesday, which is 2 * 7 = 14 articles. This took her 14 * 4 = 56 hours. In total, Meredith spent 20 + 28 + 56 = 104 hours writing articles in the three days. So the answer is 104.

Candice started with 80 post-it notes. She placed one on each of 220 cups of coffee, for a total of 220 post-it notes. She had 23 left over, so she used 80 + 220 = 300 post-it notes in total. Her package of post-it notes had 300 + 23 = 323 post-it notes. So the answer is 323.

John bought twice as many red ties as blue ties, so he bought 2 * blue ties = blue ties. He bought blue ties for $40 each, so he spent blue ties * $40 = $200 on blue ties. The red ties cost 50% more than blue ties, so they cost $40 * 1.5 = $60 each. He bought red ties for $60 each, so he spent red ties * $60 = $200 on red ties. In total, he spent $200 on blue ties + $200 on red ties = $400 on ties. So the answer is 400.
